You can use qemu-img. Here's a post on the Ubuntu forums you can adapt to fit Mint

I have done this before, the steps went like this:

  • Convert your image format to a raw (binary) format, qemu-img is the perfect tool for this.
  • Partition your target drive exactly like inside your image. I used fdisk for this.
  • Use dd to copy your raw file to your harddrive.

$ dd if=/path/to/your/raw of=/dev/sdX bs=512M

  • Use a partition repair tool to restore the original UUIDs of your partitions.

I recommend getting an empty harddrive for this, as it will map starting at the beginning of your drive.
